title: Reassess a changed blood-cell pattern before another ITP treatment
fairness: Review scope for all eight records: independently judged only the round-two after Presentation, Current update, Exhibit, Task and Options as learner-facing evidence, with the key marker disregarded for cue attacks. The authoring standard, original flags2 handoff, first review, round-two handoff and local source ledger establish review requirements, history and declared holds, not additional patient facts. Author self-checks and rationales do not establish correctness. No network, external-source re-verification, runtime/profile/feedback audit or clinical sign-off was performed. REVISE includes an unresolved key-level source hold even where wording is otherwise acceptable; PASS is editorial, not release authorization.

The two peripheral-blood options contrast with a marrow procedure, and the key contains two specimen terms, but all three are concrete diagnostic investigations of comparable length. Those differences alone do not tell a lay reader which is best. Negative viral serology and normal vitamin values are not literal exclusions of either offered blood assay. The current findings materially change the earlier isolated-thrombocytopenia premise. Blood flow cytometry and myeloid sequencing are credible neighboring investigations, but the supplied morphology raises a question about marrow assessment that neither option obviously replaces. The evolving outpatient record is credible. The five-month interval and previous steroid response provide history rather than establish a universal marrow-testing timetable. This is a diagnostic reassessment question, not permission to defer urgent treatment if a different patient has bleeding or instability; no such urgent scenario is stated here.

title: Read the acquisition record before repeating a breast study or requesting images

cues.phrase: The clinic diagram places its skin marker at 8 o'clock.
cues.why: The ultrasound record repeatedly names only 2 o'clock. Comparing two clock labels exposes an unfilled site without understanding breast imaging. With these options, the key is the only request that can obtain a new ultrasound acquisition for that site. The localization is necessary evidence; the weakness is that the option set makes elementary gap filling sufficient.

The assurance of completeness makes the archived-image choice a request for work already explicitly limited to the other marker. Combined with the site mismatch, ordinary document logic eliminates retrieval. It repairs the prior missing-export fairness problem but leaves a weak competitor.

cues.phrase: Standard and spot-compression views include both skin markers
cues.why: Repeats the specific procedure in 'Request spot-compression breast mammography' and establishes that it has already been performed at both sites. A testwise reader can discard that option as duplicate work, discard archive retrieval using the complete log, and choose the only new acquisition. This is a novelty shortcut, not majority-component convergence.

fairness: One-best-answer: targeted ultrasound is the defensible offered next radiology request for the persistent site under the supplied complete acquisition record. The item now distinguishes an unacquired site from an absent exported image. The neutral radiology-request scope means omission of biopsy is not automatically a second-key problem. Nothing here establishes that imaging ends evaluation of a persistently concerning palpable lesion.

Difficulty: easy for PGY-2/3. Finding 8 o'clock absent from a complete 2 o'clock log and selecting the only new relevant acquisition is one adequacy/gap decision, not two consequential clinical inferences. Dense tissue and the mammographic findings provide context but are not needed to defeat these two completed-work distractors.

Importance/realism: clinical-imaging concordance and site-specific acquisition are high-yield, practical breast-surgery skills. A second superficial lump explaining wrong-site imaging is plausible. A complete acquisition log in a return-visit record is possible, though the case is conspicuously arranged to expose the missed marker. The table is an acquisition record, not a diagnostic image; no image-reading difficulty should be credited.

Owner flag: partially resolved, NOT fully resolved. The exact sentence announcing that ultrasound was not performed has gone, and the completeness distinction improves fairness. The same giveaway survives functionally as an obvious site omission with two already-completed alternatives. This judgment concerns the supplied v1.r3 after fields, not an unseen or frozen B2B36 version.

Source hold touches key: NO declared key-level hold in the packet or round-two ledger. The local mapping relies on one recorded adequate ACR guideline and logical application of the site record; that is a single-source limitation, not fresh verification. Protocol realism and exact clinical ranking remain needs_clinician_review. No confident clinical inaccuracy or second offered best answer was found.
suggestions: Keep truthful site localization and acquisition completeness; deleting them would recreate the retrieval-versus-repeat ambiguity.

Replace the already-completed spot-compression foil and the plainly irrelevant archive-retrieval foil with clinically verified, same-stage alternatives that each address a genuine remaining question. Re-attack the item with medical findings hidden: if only one option still adds relevant information, the novelty cue remains.

If retaining retrieval as a competitor, it needs actual potential to contain decision-relevant information, with the acquisition record truthfully reflecting that possibility and a separate supported discriminator. Do not falsely claim completeness or withhold the log to force uncertainty.

If the intended objective remains simple wrong-site recognition, seek an explicit foundational role or use it as unscored workflow context rather than claiming routine resident-level struggle. Do not add routine MRI merely to increase complexity.

title: Do not infer pregnancy location from a falling blood result or a nondiagnostic abdominal scan

cues.phrase: Uterine cavity seen without a gestational sac; adnexal structures not resolved separately
cues.why: Describes an unfinished pelvic visualization problem just before offering a more specifically pelvic ultrasound. With a pregnancy/spotting presentation, a reader can favor completing that examination over an appendix study or tissue-removal procedure. This is a partial mechanism/gap cue, not proof a lay reader can uniquely solve the case. The observations are needed for fairness; improve the competing decisions rather than hide them.

cues.phrase: Diagnostic uterine aspiration with histopathologic assessment
cues.why: The only tissue-acquisition intervention sits beside two imaging-plus-consultation plans when the preceding record emphasizes incomplete imaging. A cautious least-invasive-first heuristic can eliminate it without resolving the falling-hCG issue. Aspiration can be a real diagnostic pathway in an appropriate context, but this stem supplies no context making it a close competitor now.

fairness: One-best-answer: transvaginal ultrasound with gynecologic assessment is a plausible best first priority among the offered plans for symptomatic pregnancy whose location is not established by the supplied abdominal scan. A falling concentration does not itself locate the pregnancy. Focal right-sided tenderness and a nonvisualized appendix keep another cause in the differential, but the question should not teach that choosing the pelvic pathway excludes appendicitis or precludes parallel surgical evaluation. The exact modality/priority comparison is held for source verification.

Difficulty: easy, despite substantial improvement over hCG assay recognition. The basic symptomatic-pregnancy/incomplete-pelvic-imaging pattern already selects the key. Deleting the early home-test history and the direction of hCG change still leaves the same strongest plan. No option actually embodies the major proposed error of treating falling hCG as permission to end location assessment. The item therefore does not require two consequential steps on its stated objective; the serial result largely decorates a familiar next-test decision.

Competitors/missing context: appendiceal MRI is a clinically conceivable alternative evaluation, but the case's pregnancy-specific symptoms and incomplete pelvic assessment favor the intended first step. Uterine aspiration would need a clearly established clinical purpose and appropriate patient context to become a close alternative. Do not infer an intention to terminate pregnancy, confirmed nonviability, or a prior adequate transvaginal examination that the text does not supply. Those missing facts weaken that distractor; they are not facts needed to justify an automatic aspiration key.

Importance/realism: recognizing a potentially consequential early-pregnancy presentation is high-value acute abdominal assessment for general surgeons and plausibly high-yield resident content. Same-day diagnostic escalation from a stable clinic visit is realistic. The words 'circulation is currently stable' are a safety summary rather than raw observations; stability and absence of generalized rigidity must not be treated as excluding an ectopic complication. No confident specific clinical falsehood is identified offline.

Owner flag: partially resolved, NOT fully resolved. This is now a consequential assessment rather than naming the pregnancy assay, but it remains too easy for the requested PGY-2/3 target. Replacement status alone does not close the original difficulty flag, and no retirement/selection action is reviewed here.

Source hold touches key: YES. Falling-hCG/location interpretation, exact transvaginal acquisition and priority over appendiceal MRI and uterine aspiration are explicitly held. This report neither resolves that hold nor certifies a universal ordering rule.
suggestions: Choose which consequential error the replacement will test. If it is interpreting an hCG trajectory, use a supported, concrete same-stage competitor whose attractiveness actually changes with that trajectory and show the observations needed to distinguish it; do not add an obviously unsafe routine-delay foil.

If the objective remains selecting the first adequate pelvic investigation, acknowledge the likely easy level and seek a deliberate safety/foundational role rather than counting raw report fields as two-step reasoning.

Remove the obsolete early home-test detail unless an offered decision truly depends on its timing. Retain symptoms, current safety information and truthful acquisition limits. Do not invent hCG thresholds, repeat intervals or management rules to manufacture difficulty.

Replace aspiration as a token invasive competitor or supply a verified clinical scenario in which it is a credible same-stage choice. Have clinical/source review resolve the exact priority over appendiceal evaluation without implying the differential closes after the keyed request.

title: Resolve an inherited calcium pattern before operative localization

cues.phrase: the mother's records show a similar longstanding pattern
cues.why: Directly supplies an inheritance narrative beside the only gene-test option. A reader can pick 'Calcium-sensing receptor gene assay' by family-to-genetics association without interpreting PTH, urinary clearance or skeletal data. The family observation is legitimate clinical evidence; its uniquely matching option creates the shortcut.

cues.phrase: Earlier adult records show calcium in the same mildly elevated band
cues.why: Reinforces a longstanding trait rather than a new operative problem and, in combination with the mother's similar record, rehearses the inherited-condition rationale for the sole genetic investigation. It is not an independent answer proof, but strengthens the family-wording shortcut.

fairness: One-best-answer: genetic clarification is the strongest offered direction given the combined biochemical, urinary and family findings. The local source mappings specifically treat the low clearance ratio as supportive rather than diagnostic. No competing listed test is confidently equally good here: localization assumes a sufficiently established operative disease, while a PTH-related peptide assay addresses a different mechanistic question from the nonsuppressed-PTH pattern. This is not a claim that those tests have no clinical uses.

Precision: the named calcium-sensing receptor assay is a concrete genetic option, but it should not be taught as exhaustive genetic evaluation or as a definitive rule-out if negative. The displayed question does not explicitly make either claim. Do not infer a confirmed inherited disorder, a particular mutation or a universal no-surgery rule from this single ratio/family pattern.

Difficulty: easy for the requested PGY-2/3 target. The low-clearance, longstanding familial hypercalcemia pattern is a familiar recognition cluster, and the only genetic option is available before interpreting most of the data. Naming the likely inherited process and choosing its corresponding assay is not two consequential steps in this option set. Diagnostic clarification before localization is a valuable intended sequencing distinction, but the PTH-related peptide foil and strong family cue let the learner bypass it.

Importance/realism: avoiding an inappropriate parathyroid operation by distinguishing an inherited calcium pattern from PHPT is high-yield and practically important endocrine-surgery learning. The referral, paired collection and family records are plausible outpatient information. Normal renal/vitamin-D findings and absent thiazide use help interpret the ratio rather than literally delete any offered test. The old DXA acquisition and hip-prosthesis details are largely residual context for this downstream question; they do not increase its difficulty.

Owner flag: fully resolved at the visible paired-wording level for the original DXA-before-operation concern. Referral and baseline assessment were already ordered together, and the new reason to clarify the diagnosis is the subsequent urine/family information, not a requirement for an abnormal DXA. This changes the scored objective rather than demonstrating that the old age-criterion question became harder. Runtime gating, actual referral timing and mixed-version composition were not audited.

Source hold touches key: NO declared key-level hold in the packet or round-two ledger. Recorded PARAT/Fifth Workshop claims support the inherited pattern, ratio limitation and genetic/family evaluation; duplicate Fifth Workshop source IDs are one publication. The G05-staging hardware/radius hold is a separate paired-item hold, not the basis of this genetic key. No fresh verification of the exact assay wording or clinical approval is claimed.
suggestions: Keep clinically meaningful family and urinary observations; do not hide family history solely to evade cue detection. Rebuild the competitors so family-to-gene matching cannot solve the item without interpreting the collection and biochemical context.

Replace the weak PTH-related peptide foil with a supported close alternative at the same diagnostic decision stage, such as a genuinely relevant reassessment of a documented collection or biochemical uncertainty if that uncertainty is actually present. Do not invent a collection problem or introduce a new one solely in the rationale.

For a harder version, make a verified observation change whether inherited-disease clarification or operative localization is appropriate, and show that observation rather than announcing the diagnosis. Reapply the deletion test: family wording alone should not select a unique option, and changing the decisive record should change the best plan.

Verify the intended scope of the named gene assay and preserve uncertainty about a negative or nonconfirmatory result. Keep the parallel referral chronology and review the composed staging/follow-up pair before accepting either into a different header or sequence.

I do not identify a confident alternative key, and I do not substitute an assumed densitometry protocol for the missing source confirmation.

Correct acquisition in the presence of an implant is practical, although this exact hip-by-radius matrix has narrower resident payoff than deciding whether the study changes diagnosis or management. No current ABSITE outline has been verified, and it should not be presented as proof that an exact densitometry technical detail is high-yield.

If retaining a routine resident application question, use a verified acquisition/interpretation problem that changes a real clinical plan and compare credible orders at that stage. Avoid merely adding another component to the matrix. Keep referral independent of the DXA result.

title: Use the testing population at collection, not the later referral setting
fairness: Cue attack: no exploitable wording, option-length, grammar, category, absolute-word or convergence cue found. One-best-answer: independent arithmetic confirms 45/(45+19) = 70.3125%, uniquely supporting about 70%. The competing 92% is 180/(180+16) from the ICU row; 90% is 45/(45+5), sensitivity; 5% is (45+5)/1000, the pre-admission reference-positive proportion. Each numeric distractor represents a coherent cohort or denominator error. No clinical threshold or empirical assay performance is inferred.

Difficulty: moderate. Two consequential steps are required: select the population at specimen collection rather than the later discussion setting, then condition on the positive PCR result. The table is necessary and the plausible alternate percentages prevent a wording-only answer. Residents fluent in diagnostic-test tables may find it easy; this remains a qualitative prediction rather than measured difficulty.

Fairness boundary: the answer is the audit PPV for the original specimen under the question's constructed comparison. It is not an individualized probability of current postoperative colonization, invasive MRSA disease or treatment benefit. The task says 'Using this audit', which sufficiently bounds the exercise. No additional patient-specific risk estimate is needed for this mathematical question.

Importance/realism: interpreting diagnostic tests using the appropriate population is useful, plausibly high-yield general-surgery/ABSITE numeracy. A pre-admission specimen discussed after ICU care is plausible. A post-pancreatic-cancer visit focused on a screening PPV is somewhat contrived, and the cancer location adds little, but those minor contextual weaknesses do not undermine the single key or two-step task.

title: Choose representative node tissue and specimen handling after a limited aspirate

cues.phrase: Scattered cell groups; no intact nodal tissue pattern in the sections
cues.why: Emphasizes lack of intact tissue, encouraging a get-more-intact-tissue heuristic toward excision. This is necessary specimen information, not a teaching sentence, and it does not uniquely select the key without interpreting the methods. In combination with the dual-processing choices, however, the largest/more-comprehensive specimen plan becomes a testwise favorite.

cues.phrase: Predominantly nonviable cells; no interpretable clonality result
cues.why: Beside fresh/fixed versus formalin labels, ordinary association of fresh with viable favors both fresh/fixed choices. The observation legitimately identifies an unresolved study, but a fresh label alone does not explain the prior failure or guarantee viability in the next sample. This is a partial cue, not a reason to remove the failed result.

Combines the apparently larger specimen with both processing streams. The balanced matrix prevents majority-component convergence, but does not prevent a choose-more-tissue-and-more-tests shortcut when no competing burden or adequacy tradeoff is evident. This is a weaker comprehensiveness cue than the prior solid-versus-debris giveaway and still requires some familiarity with biopsy terminology.

fairness: One-best-answer: excision with planned histologic and ancillary allocation is a plausible strongest plan for this accessible node after limited same-target sampling. The mobile/superficial anatomy is genuine procedural context, not by itself a gratuitous permission sentence. A well-planned core with appropriate allocation remains a clinically credible competitor. Whether the supplied facts establish a sufficiently strong preference for excision is precisely the held comparison; I cannot certify unique superiority or assert that core is equally good without that verification.

Option ambiguity: 'with formalin fixation' does not explicitly say the entire specimen is fixed. A fresh/fixed plan also includes formalin-fixed tissue. The intended contrast can be inferred from the matrix, but the after labels do not literally make the processing options mutually exclusive. The rationale outside the after fields cannot supply the missing whole-specimen qualifier. This is a concrete fairness repair, not merely a desire for longer labels.

Specimen limitation: the previous flow result establishes failure to obtain an interpretable result, but does not identify why cells were nonviable. The text must not be read as proving that formalin caused that failure or that any fresh allocation will solve it. The significance of EBV in blood or scattered cells likewise does not by itself provide a complete tissue classification. No exact diagnosis or treatment is established here.

Difficulty: moderate, with two meaningful operations: interpret what the prior same-node specimen leaves unanswered, then combine a representative method with handling suited to the remaining studies. Unlike round one, both methods address the solid node, so there are no waste-target foils. The processing ambiguity and unverified method preference are not counted as desirable difficulty. The more-is-better shortcut still lowers discrimination.

Importance/realism: obtaining adequate nodal tissue and coordinating specimen handling are practically important surgical responsibilities and plausible high-yield resident learning. The transplant setting is a credible reason for careful classification. The exact PTLD method preference is more specialized than the general sampling principle and needs hematopathology input. The exhibit is a sampling/laboratory record, not an image-reading task.

Owner flag: fully resolved in the broad requested sense that each answer now specifies a biopsy method and a processing plan rather than generic care coordination. The narrower whole-specimen allocation ambiguity remains a new repair. Specificity does not establish clinical ranking or source adequacy, and this report makes no claim that the candidate is live.

Source hold touches key: YES. The accessible-node excision-versus-core ranking and fresh/fixed allocation are both explicitly held. Existing general PTLD tissue and neck-core claims do not independently validate this complete plan. The hold remains open; no universal excision rule or categorical failure of core biopsy is accepted.
suggestions: Make processing choices explicitly nonoverlapping and parallel. For example, use 'Excisional biopsy; portions fresh and formalin-fixed', 'Core biopsy; portions fresh and formalin-fixed', 'Excisional biopsy; entire specimen formalin-fixed' and 'Core biopsy; entire specimen formalin-fixed', subject to verification of the intended local handling protocol. The whole-specimen qualifier is decision information, not an explanatory insult to a distractor.

Resolve the held excision/core ranking and required ancillary handling with permitted guidance and hematopathology review. Identify the exact supported observation making a properly allocated core less appropriate here; do not reject it merely because it yields less tissue.

Preserve the same-target history, observed cell-block limitations, failed flow result and procedural anatomy. Do not replace them with a summary such as inconclusive aspirate or a teaching sentence that architecture requires excision.

If the verified ranking remains insufficiently discriminating, build the next version around a genuine patient/specimen tradeoff rather than a universally larger specimen plus more processing. Do not invent surgical risk, a laboratory requirement or the cause of prior cell death to make one option win.
